claims.text: The modeled nanoparticles are random equiatomic FeNiCrCoCu solid solutions with 20 at.% of each element.
The initial nanoparticles have an FCC lattice with a 3.52 Å lattice parameter.
Premelting and melting are governed by an inverse-radius two-phase transition mechanism.
Element-specific energetic inhomogeneities drive the proposed transition mechanism.
Fe atoms have local potential energies approximately 0.5 eV higher than those of the other constituent elements.
Cu's lower elemental melting point contributes to its early atomistic mobility.
Fe and Cu develop preferential mobility at approximately 900 K.
The preferential early mobility begins in the outer two to three atomic layers.
Element-specific diffusion subsequently progresses from the surface into the particle core.
Early Fe and Cu diffusion sets the stage for, and helps determine, nanoparticle melting.
Melting occurs through competition between solid and liquid phases rather than through a stable surface-liquid shell.
Melting temperature increases with particle radius.
As particle size increases, the melting temperature approaches a bulk melting limit of 2184 K.
Fe and Cu exhibit higher mean-square displacements before the complete melting transition.
Premelting and melting occur without significant persistent chemical clustering.
Element-specific premelting is negligible at a radius of approximately 5 Å and becomes more pronounced in larger nanoparticles.
The proposed mechanism applies to particle radii of approximately 5–40 Å under the specified simulation and heating protocol.
Selective Fe and Cu mobility may depend on the interatomic potential, initial atomic configuration, and heating rate.
Short-range clustering at the smallest sizes may affect early diffusion.

contradictions.description: The protocol is described as NVE while also using velocity rescaling during heating. Repeated velocity rescaling changes particle energy and is not strictly microcanonical unless NVE refers only to intervals between rescaling operations.
The predicted outcome says early enhanced Fe and Cu mobility occurs in all cases, whereas the boundary says element-specific premelting should be negligible at the smallest size, approximately 5 Å.
